input.quote: 10. NONASSIGNABILITY. Neither party shall assign, transfer, or subcontract this Agreement or any of its obligations hereunder without the other party's express, prior written consent, which will not be unreasonably withheld.
input.rationale: The only assignment provision (§ 10) is mutual and applies a reasonable-consent standard, but it requires Contractor's consent for every transfer, including assignment to a Company affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets. The fallback position requires a right to assign to successors (on notice, without consent), so the clause falls short of the fallback on a material term. Positively, there is no change-of-control trigger anywhere in the Agreement — § 6 termination rights are limited to convenience (no open SOW) and uncured material breach — so no Vendor exit or re-pricing right arises on our change of control. Minimal redline adds the affiliate/successor carve-out for Company; we did not add the "no assignment to a Customer competitor" restriction on Contractor, which is a preferred-position refinement only.

proposal.summary: Add Company carve-out to assign to affiliates and M&A successors without consent
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added a customary carve-out allowing Company to assign to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets without consent, so ordinary corporate reorganizations do not require Contractor's approval. Contractor's assignment rights remain subject to consent as drafted; if helpful, we can instead make the successor right mutual on written notice.
